identity.title: To Infinity and Beyond: Tool-Use Unlocks Length Generalization in State Space Models

problem.claim: The paper examines whether State Space Models can accurately handle truly long-form generation and generalize to problems of increasing length or complexity.

gap.claim: The authors identify a theoretical limitation: SSMs cannot accurately solve any formally defined truly long-form generation problem, despite their claimed long-context efficiency advantage.

contributions.claim: A theoretical result characterizing a class of truly long-form generation problems that SSMs cannot accurately solve.

A tool-augmented SSM framework in which interactive external-tool access, together with problem-dependent training data, is proposed to mitigate this limitation and support arbitrary length/complexity generalization for tractable problems.
An empirical demonstration of tool-augmented SSMs on arithmetic, reasoning, and coding tasks with reported length generalization.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their approach by combining SSMs with interactive external tools and problem-dependent training data to target arbitrary problem-length and complexity generalization.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report a theoretical result that SSMs cannot accurately solve any problem in their formally defined class of truly long-form generation problems.
The authors report that, with suitable tool access and problem-dependent training data, SSMs can learn to solve any tractable problem and generalize to arbitrary problem length and complexity.
The authors report remarkable length generalization by tool-augmented SSMs across arithmetic, reasoning, and coding tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: SSMs are presented as efficient Transformer alternatives for long-context and long-form generation because they use fixed-size memory and linear computational scaling.
The paper introduces a theoretical impossibility result for accurately solving truly long-form generation problems.
Interactive access to external tools is proposed as a way to mitigate the limitation.
With appropriate tools and problem-dependent training data, the authors report arbitrary length/complexity generalization for tractable problems.
Tool-augmented SSMs are reported to generalize in arithmetic, reasoning, and coding tasks, motivating their potential use in interactive and agentic settings.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a limitation result with a conditional remedy: suitable tool access and problem-dependent training data are specified before the broad generalization claim.

lessons.interpretation: This links the scope of a capability claim to explicit enabling conditions rather than presenting the method as universally sufficient.
lessons.application: When proposing a capability extension, state the limiting result, then name the required interface and data conditions before claiming broader generalization.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the proposed conditions are not yet defined well enough to be tested or reproduced.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide the formal definition of “truly long-form,” the exact tools or training data, or the meaning of “accurately.”
Task datasets, evaluation metrics, comparison baselines, and quantitative results for the reported demonstrations are unspecified.
The scope of “any tractable problem” and the conditions for arbitrary generalization are not detailed.
